newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Rail pressure group Save Our Railways has calculated the profits and potential losses of all 25 privatised rail companies. South West Trains is potentially the most profitable. The train company which cut so many of its drivers it did not have enough to maintain services, stands to make up to 478m stg during its seven year franchise.

Chances of meeting the target for monetary union in 1999 look increasingly hopeful as an updated method for calculating GDP, means that member countries may be able to meet the more difficult of the Maastricht Treaty's four criteria for countries who want to take part in EMU. The toughest of these criteria is that public sector deficits should not exceed 3 percent of gross domestic product.
- DOLLAR SOARS TO FOUR-YEAR HIGH AGAINST YEN
For the first time in four years, despite the best efforts of Japanese finance officials the dollar climbed to 125 yen.
There has been a further development in the Busang gold scandal with Indonesia sacking the top mines department official overseeing the Bre-X project, Kuntoro Mangkusubroto.

Due to demand from the world's industrial producers for base metals such as copper, tin, aluminium and zinc, exceeding supply, prices are set to increase. The future for the gold market is uncertain. The upturn in the base metals market has helped by falling interest rates, increased industrial activity worldwide and growing infrastructure investment from the developing economies.
